own_solution.law: Convert the dimensions to SI: a = 0.015 m and ell = 0.40 m. Then L = μ₀N²πa²/ell = 0.00142163 H and I₀ = V/R₁ = 3 A. During discharge, L di/dt = -R₂i, so Q = ∫₀∞R₂i²dt = LI₀²/2 = 0.00639735 J = 6.39735 mJ. An aiding additional emf q changes this to Q(q) = L[(12 + q)/4]²/2.
assumptions: Use the stated long, air-cored solenoid model with negligible winding resistance.
The second resistor has finite positive resistance.
The ideal discharge circuit dissipates the initial magnetic energy entirely in the second resistor.

notes: All certified answers agree with the physics in the specified target unit mJ. For additional emfs of 3.2, 7.5 and 11 V, the energies are respectively 10.2642, 16.893 and 23.5014 mJ. Each listed discharge resistance gives 6.39735 mJ; resistance changes the decay time but cancels from the integrated heat. The stated minimal pairs preserve 7.5 V and change only the causal attachment or timing. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies T212D and TC1E1 as numeral-free controls, rather than claiming that they preserve their twins' number and unit. The locked pass-1 numerical answers were expressed in J and are equivalent to these answers in mJ. The inductance relation requires converting the input lengths from cm to m.
